name: Creative Writing With AI Parts Marked
title: Creative Writing With AI Parts Marked
answer: Creative writing with AI parts marked means students may use AI to generate drafts or suggestions, but they must show which parts came from the tool and how they used it. The student's own choices, not the machine's, must shape the final piece. This matters because creative writing is where students are most tempted to let AI do the work, and marking AI's contribution keeps the process honest while still allowing AI to spark creativity.

crumbs.name: Reading and Writing, Kindergarten Through 12th Grade

sections.body: This idea addresses the tension in creative writing, where AI can either replace student effort or support it. The machine can offer a draft, and the student reshapes it, as in the Finnish poetry study described in the chapter. The key is that the student's choices shape the final piece, not the machine's. Marking AI's contribution, by highlighting suggested lines or adding a short note, makes the student's own work visible. It also turns AI use into an honest part of the writing process rather than a hidden shortcut.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, a student can ask an AI tool for a draft or suggestions, then reshape that material and mark any lines the tool suggested. The text gives one grade band example: in a three month program, 82 upper elementary students in Hong Kong wrote digital stories about AI. That project built both writing skill and AI literacy. For any assignment, the student can add a short note explaining how they used AI, which makes their own work visible. This matches the AI use levels from Chapter 3, where a teacher marks what is allowed on each assignment.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text cites two studies. In the Finnish poetry study at the start of the chapter, students who revised more wrote better poems (Kangasharju et al., 2022). In a three month program, 82 upper elementary students in Hong Kong wrote digital stories about AI, and their stories showed real understanding of how AI works (Ng et al., 2022). The text does not give a separate evidence label for this idea. It presents these findings as support for the approach.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The main risk is that students let AI do the work in creative writing. The text says the student's choices, not the machine's, must shape the final piece. AI's contribution should be marked, either by highlighting lines the tool suggested or by adding a short note explaining how it was used. The decision about what AI use is allowed stays with the teacher, who marks what is allowed on each assignment, as in the AI use levels from Chapter 3. The student still decides how to revise and how to explain their use, so the final piece remains their own visible work.
